In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of the bias in the air mass factors (AMFs) of space-borne observations of tropospheric NO2 that results from neglecting lightning NO2 in the a prioris.
quantifying the effect of adding modeled lightning NO2 to a priori profiles on tropospheric NO2 air mass factors.
the quantification of the effect that lightning NO2 has on the retrieval of tropospheric NO2 columns from space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of modeled lightning NO2 to a priori profiles reduces the bias in tropospheric NO2 columns from space-based sensors by up to 35 % over the central and eastern US in late spring and early fall.
a simulation without NO2 produced by lightning underestimates the AMF by 25 %, and that adding 500 to 650 mol NO2 flash−1 reduces this bias.
the bias in the air mass factor for NO2 observations over the United States in the summer can be as much as 35 % when lightning NO2 production is not included in the a prioris.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have quantified how much bias in the AMFs for tropospheric NO2 columns can occur due to the omission of modeled lightning NO2 in the a prioris for OMI and future geostationary satellite measurements.
the addition of lightning NO2 to a priori profiles is essential for accurate retrievals of UT NO2 columns from satellite observations, particularly from geostationary sensors.
the addition of lightning NO2 in the a prioric profiles improves the accuracy of the NO2 column by reducing the bias in the air mass factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of lightning NO2 on the AMF is significant and must be considered when using satellite observations to constrain the lightning NO2 source in chemical transport models.
the impact of lightning NO2 on the AMF is large and that it must be accounted for in the OMI a priori profiles to avoid significant bias in tropospheric NO2 columns.
lightning NO2 is a significant contributor to UT NO2 and should be included when simulating the NO2 vertical distribution for satellite NO2 observations.
